title: Prescriptions from Out-of-State Practitioners
subtopic: Presentation windows and the verification gate
learning_objectives: Choose the presentation window by the schedule of the substance, not by the federal refill clock.
Apply the mandatory verification gate before filling an out-of-state Schedule III through V prescription.

quick_review.text: An authorized out-of-state practitioner's Schedule III through VI prescription may be filled in Massachusetts only if it was issued within the preceding 30 days.
Massachusetts applies a five-day presentation window to out-of-state Schedule II prescriptions instead, under separate subsections with their own issuing-state conditions.
A Schedule III through V prescription on this pathway must be verified by the pharmacist, and may not be filled if verification cannot be obtained.
Where the out-of-state prescription is oral and in Schedules III through V, the pharmacist records having requested the practitioner's written prescription.
The Schedule II narcotic route reaches only a practitioner registered in Maine or a state contiguous with the commonwealth, and requires authentication and verification before the fill.

decision_logic.condition: An out-of-state practitioner's prescription is presented.
decision_logic.action: Identify the schedule first: Schedule III through VI runs on the 30-day window, Schedule II on the five-day window.

decision_logic.condition: The out-of-state prescription is in Schedules III through V.
decision_logic.action: Verify it by telephone or other means before filling, and do not fill it if verification cannot be obtained.

decision_logic.condition: The out-of-state Schedule III-V prescription was communicated orally.
decision_logic.action: Record that you requested the practitioner deliver or mail the written prescription within seven days or the shorter federal period.

ma_vs_federal.text: The federal six-month Schedule III-IV clock does not license an out-of-state prescription that Massachusetts no longer treats as fillable; the presentation window is the earlier gate.

exceptions.text: The five-day Schedule II window sits in separate subsections that also carry their own conditions on which issuing states qualify, so it is not simply a shorter version of the same rule.
Separate delivery provisions govern certain out-of-state residents, so the narcotic route is not simply the nonnarcotic route with a different list of states.

timing_deadlines.event: Out-of-state Schedule III through VI prescription
timing_deadlines.consequence: Outside the window this pathway does not authorize the fill at all.

timing_deadlines.timeframe: Presented within five days of issue
timing_deadlines.consequence: The 30-day figure does not carry across to Schedule II.

timing_deadlines.event: Practitioner delivery of an out-of-state oral Schedule III-V written follow-up
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Within 7 days or the shorter federal period
timing_deadlines.consequence: The period governs the practitioner's delivery or mailing, not the pharmacist's recording.

forms_records.text: On the out-of-state oral Schedule III-V pathway the pharmacist records having requested the practitioner's written prescription.

role_duties.duty: Verify an out-of-state Schedule III through V prescription before filling it, and refuse the fill where verification cannot be obtained.

common_traps.text: Carrying the 30-day out-of-state window to a Schedule II prescription accepts one that Massachusetts allows only within five days of issue.
Filling an out-of-state Schedule III-V prescription on the federal six-month clock skips both the presentation window and the verification gate.
Treating the seven-day follow-up period as the pharmacist's deadline reverses the timed event.
